subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 28-year-old woman with sickle cell disease is evaluated for worsening fatigue and scleral icterus. Laboratory studies show hemoglobin 7.4 g/dL, reticulocytes 9%, total bilirubin 3.6 mg/dL with a direct fraction of 0.4 mg/dL, elevated lactate dehydrogenase, and low haptoglobin. Serum liver enzymes are normal. Her jaundice is attributed to increased breakdown of hemoglobin by macrophages in the spleen and liver.
question: Which of the following is a direct product of the reaction that converts heme to biliverdin in this patient?
explanation_correct: Heme oxygenase, located in reticuloendothelial cells of the spleen, liver, and bone marrow, opens the heme ring to produce biliverdin while releasing carbon monoxide and ferrous iron. Biliverdin is then reduced to unconjugated bilirubin by biliverdin reductase. The carbon monoxide generated by this pathway contributes to the small amount of carboxyhemoglobin normally present in blood.

explanation_incorrect.A: Bilirubin is produced from biliverdin by biliverdin reductase, so it is a product of the next reaction rather than a direct product of heme oxygenase.
explanation_incorrect.C: Urobilinogen is formed in the intestine when conjugated bilirubin is reduced by gut bacteria, several steps downstream of heme degradation.
explanation_incorrect.D: Stercobilin is the oxidized product of urobilinogen that gives feces their color and forms much later in the pathway.
explanation_incorrect.E: Bilirubin diglucuronide is conjugated bilirubin produced in hepatocytes by UGT1A1 after bilirubin has been taken up from plasma.

educationalObjective: Heme oxygenase converts heme to biliverdin with release of carbon monoxide and iron; biliverdin is subsequently reduced to bilirubin by biliverdin reductase.
